description: Hi! I'm Juliana, an Information Systems student from Brazil interested in AI, data science, and environmental challenges. I work with Python, data analysis, statistics, and machine learning. For NASA Space Apps, I'm developing a coral reef monitoring project using satellite and ocean data to explore reef conditions and identify patterns associated with thermal stress.
summary:
ReefScope is an interactive dashboard developed to explore coral reef conditions and investigate environmental trends over time. It combines historical benthic composition data from NASA's CORAL mission with sea surface temperature and thermal stress indicators from NOAA Coral Reef Watch.
The dashboard includes four main sections: an overview of the study area, reef composition analysis, environmental monitoring, and an early warning system. It allows users to explore coral, algae, and sand class probabilities, visualize historical sea surface temperature records, investigate regional trends, and monitor bleaching-related indicators.
By bringing these datasets together, CoralWatch supports the investigation of Earth system trends, helping users understand how environmental conditions vary across regions and over time. This is important because monitoring changes in ocean temperature and reef conditions can provide valuable context for studying coral reef vulnerability and the environmental pressures affecting these ecosystems.
details:
ReefScope is an interactive dashboard designed to explore coral reef conditions and investigate environmental trends over time. It brings together two complementary data sources: NASA's CORAL mission, which provides information on reef composition, and NOAA Coral Reef Watch, which provides sea surface temperature and thermal stress indicators.

The dashboard is organized into four sections. Overview introduces the study area and the available datasets. Reef Composition explores coral, algae, and sand class probabilities from NASA CORAL observations. Environmental Monitoring displays recent environmental conditions and historical sea surface temperature records, allowing users to compare regions and investigate long-term trends. Early Warning System presents NOAA's Bleaching Alert Area classifications alongside thermal indicators such as HotSpot and Degree Heating Weeks (DHW).

We developed the dashboard using Python and Streamlit, with libraries for data processing, visualization, and statistical analysis. The trend analysis uses the Theil-Sen estimator and Mann-Kendall test, with Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment for multiple comparisons. The project also includes data filtering, CSV exports, and automated tests.

One of the main challenges was bringing together datasets with different formats, spatial footprints, and observation periods without implying relationships that the data does not establish. We preserved the original regional identifiers, kept missing observations visible instead of interpolating them, and considered differences in data coverage when interpreting trends.

CoralWatch's main benefit is making environmental data easier to explore and interpret. Rather than presenting only current conditions, it gives users a way to examine historical changes and compare environmental indicators across regions. Its intended impact is to support environmental awareness and data-informed investigation of coral reef vulnerability. The dashboard does not predict bleaching events or diagnose coral mortality; it provides information that can help users investigate the conditions associated with reef stress.

The creative aspect of the project is the integration of reef composition, historical environmental data, statistical trend analysis, and early warning indicators in a single interface, turning separate datasets into a more accessible tool for exploring changes in coral reef environments.
